title: Using Sahayak with a disability
note: SAMPLE DATA. Written to exercise the grounded-agent pattern for a demo. Every entry here is illustrative and has not been reviewed by a subject expert. entries.content: Open the Accessibility panel in the sidebar (or the More sheet on a phone) and turn on Large text. It increases text size and spacing across every module and is remembered on this device.
Voice mode lets you ask a question by speaking and hear the answer read back. Turn it on in the Accessibility panel. Where the browser does not support speech, typing still works everywhere.
Every control can be reached with the Tab key and activated with Enter or Space. A 'Skip to main content' link is the first thing Tab reaches on each page. The focus outline shows where you are.

Answers appear in a live region, so a screen reader announces them as they arrive. Numbers that count up expose their final value, not the intermediate ticks. Images that carry meaning have text alternatives.
Sahayak follows the high-contrast setting of your device. When it is on, decorative effects are switched off and borders are drawn at full strength.
Questions you have already asked in a session can be answered again from the device without a connection. Turn on Offline mode in the Accessibility panel to see how the app behaves without a network.
Use the EN / हि switch in the sidebar or the top bar. It keeps you on the same screen and remembers the choice for next time. Every screen exists in both languages.
The national helpline for persons with disabilities is 1800-111-11 (Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities). District Disability Rehabilitation Centres provide in-person assistance.
